title: timeline-hole-detection-nsight-scan-apr-2028
content:
Objective:
Investigate recurring idle gaps / "timeline holes" observed in Nsight System traces during steady-state inference on dedicated GPU pools. These holes appear between kernel launches and correlate with latency tail events for long requests (seq_len >= 1024). Aim: root-cause (s scheduling, async-copy overlap, cudaGraph fragmentation, or host-side enqueue jitter) and propose mitigations that do not regress p50 latency or throughput for typical throughput workloads.

Quick summary of key findings:
- Traces captured with nsys show repeated 0.4–1.6 ms gaps on the GPU timeline where SMs are idle between small kernels in the generation loop. These are not NVTX gaps — the host is queuing kernels but there is a measurable gap on the device.
- Nsight Compute sampling on representative kernels reports achieved_occupancy ~0.4–0.55 (for our Llama-like attention kernels at batch 8, seq 1024) while theoretical occupancy could be ~0.75 given register/shared memory usage.
- Primary contributors to stalls (per kernel-level stall reason breakdown): 45% memory dependency/backpressure, 20% execution dependency, 15% idle (no warps eligible), remainder from synchronization.
- CUDA graph instantiation / replay reduces host-side enqueue jitter but shows more fragmented kernel groupings: we see many short-lived graphs (created per microbatch) destroying coalescing opportunities.
- Top-of-stack hypothesis: combination of small kernel granularity + asynchronous copy bursts + suboptimal stream/priority assignment causing kernel interleaving that leaves short windows where no warps are eligible.

Environment / test harness:
- HW: A100-SXM-80GB (dedicated pool node), driver 535.xx, CUDA 12.2.
- Model: redwood-quick-6b quantized FP16, generation loop using block-attention kernels and a small fused FFN.
- Runtime config: microbatch_size=1, batch_size=8 (accumulated), kv_cache enabled, prefetch_async=true, cuda_graph_replay=true (per-request graph), stream_priority: default.
- Repro commands: 
  - Capture system timeline:
    nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --output=run_timeline --sample=none --force-overwrite --target-processes=all --stats=true --duration=60s -- python tools/inference_benchmark.py --model redwood-quick-6b --batch 8 --seq 1024 --requests 1000
  - Capture per-kernel metrics (Nsight Compute):
    ncu --target-processes all --metrics achieved_occupancy,sm_efficiency,warp_issue_efficiency,eligible_warps,sm_active_cycles --section "LaunchStats" --launch-skip 10 --launch-count 200 --output ncu_run

What we observed in the timeline (selected slices):
- Repeating pattern every token step: small memcpy H2D (~10–40 us), then kernel A (attention qk product) ~150–250 us, kernel B (softmax+scaling) ~20–40 us, kernel C (fused matmul for value) ~80–120 us, then a gap 0.4–1.2 ms before next token's kernels begin.
- The gap grows with sequence length when KV cache reads dominate; for cold-start tokens the gap is lower (~200–400 us).
- When cuda_graph_replay=false (pure stream enqueue), gaps persist but are slightly higher variance; when cuda_graph_replay=true (per-request graph), gaps are narrower but appear more frequently, indicating that per-request graphs increase short-kernel fragmentation.
- Switching to a model variant with a slightly larger fused-kernel (experimental fused-attention-v2) reduces the number of gaps by ~60% and increases achieved_occupancy to ~0.68. However, p99 latency occasionally increases due to single-kernel tail (very long kernel durations interact poorly with retry/backpressure in our scheduler).

Detailed metrics (representative):
- Kernel A (q*k): achieved_occupancy 0.43, sm_efficiency 61%, warp_issue_efficiency 47%, avg duration 190 us.
- Kernel B (softmax): achieved_occupancy 0.27, sm_efficiency 44%, avg duration 28 us.
- Kernel C (v matmul): achieved_occupancy 0.52, sm_efficiency 70%, avg duration 96 us.
- Fraction of timeline idle gaps: ~18% of token-steps had >=500 us idle gap; ~3% had >=1.2 ms.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel granularity too fine: many short kernels cause scheduling churn and increase the chance of idle gaps between kernels.
2) CUDA graph fragmentation: per-request graphs prevent kernel coalescing that the driver could otherwise do when kernels are enqueued on the same stream.
3) Async copy bursts: pinned host buffers and overlapping H2D for KV cache reads create temporary memory subsystem saturation causing memory dependency stalls.
4) Stream priority / scheduler ordering: kernels from different model components or background tasks interfere and preempt/poke gaps.
5) Host-side wakeup jitter: unlikely primary for gaps > 400 us but still contributes for some long-tail events.

Repro experiments to run (quick, prioritized):
- E1 (Medium effort): Run the same workload with a single fused kernel option (fused-attention-v2) to measure impact on gaps and occupancy. Metric: % token-steps with gap >= 500 us. Owner: Marta. Target: 2028-04-20.
- E2 (Low effort): Disable cuda_graph_replay (fall back to stream enqueue) and compare gap distribution and p50/p99 latency. Owner: Samir. Target: 2028-04-17.
- E3 (Medium): Change cudaGraph strategy to per-sequence instantiation (instantiate once per sequence length bucket) instead of per-request. Measure graph instantiation cost and gap counts. Owner: Ethan. Target: 2028-04-24.
- E4 (Low): Increase stream priority of inference streams and deprioritize background housekeeping (checkpointing, memstats). Quick test to detect interference. Owner: Priya. Target: 2028-04-18.
- E5 (Experiment): Add a micro-sleep coalescing shim on host that intentionally pads 200us between kernel groups to see if that improves coalescing on the device (counterintuitive but measures scheduler behavior). Owner: Marta+Samir. Target: 2028-04-22.

Suggested mitigations (short-term and longer-term):
- Short-term: try fused kernels where possible (observed occupancy gains). Disable per-request cuda graphs until we have a per-seq-length bucket strategy. Reduce concurrent H2D bursts by introducing a simple async copy rate limiter.
- Medium-term: implement a graph coalescer in the runtime that will combine compatible per-microbatch graphs into a single graph per step where possible.
- Long-term: explore persistent kernels or a streaming persistent-thread model for attention that keeps warps eligible across token steps (requires careful tradeoffs with preemption and multi-tenant pods).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why is softmax kernel occupancy so low? Is it register/spill limited or memory-latency bound? Need ncu source-level analysis.
- Are there driver-level heuristics that cause stream serialization on heavy H2D load? Need to collaborate with infra to test on an isolated node with synthetic H2D patterns.
- How do these patterns change on different GPU generations (H100, L40)? We should run comparative traces.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Run E2 (disable cuda_graph_replay) and post results in the Jira ticket ENG-4821. (Samir)
- Capture NCU source-level metrics for softmax to determine register pressure and memory instruction breakdown. (Ethan)
- Prototype per-sequence-length graph instantiation and measure instantiation overhead vs gap reduction. (Marta + Priya)
- Add NVTX markers in runtime around graph creation/launch path to correlate host-side timings. (Priya)

Notes to reviewers:
- Traces and NCU outputs are large — see linked_artifacts for raw captures. The shorthand metrics above are aggregated across several runs; we should re-run experiments for reproducibility before making infra changes.
- This doc is intentionally a working note: contains hypotheses and experiment plan. Please add comments inline in Confluence or ping in #eng-runtime.

Appendix (quick commands and tips):
- Force CUDA graphs to be disabled at runtime: set REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1
- Enable verbose NVTX around graph work: REDWOOD_NVTX_V=2
- Nsight capture SNIPPET command for short window:
  nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-forked-processes=true --output slice_run --duration=10s -- python tools/inference_benchmark.py --single_sequence --model redwood-quick-6b --batch 8 --seq 1024

If you want anything moved into a canonical runbook or tests created in infra/capture-tests, call it out here and I'll schedule a tile in the sprint.

-- Priya
